page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector instructions. This instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, providing 307 GB of local disk capacity alongside Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by high memory capacity but relatively constrained processing speeds. The instance registers weak performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as in Passmark CPU and database operations. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks fall into the bottom 25%, though the Passmark memory score achieves an average rating. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-4ds_v4 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU throughput. The inclusion of 307 GB of local storage adds value for applications requiring temporary data caching. Given these characteristics, this server is best suited for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads, such as caching layers, small-scale database hosting, and basic text processing tasks.
